synopsis: The booklet identifies DO-178C as the software standard for airborne systems, placing it within aerospace practice that accepts validated simulation and prior evidence under strict similarity rules [f14660, f14653]. DO-330 is its tool-qualification supplement or companion, addressing tools whose output is relied on without further checking [f14661, f15367]. However, Chapter 10 reports that the research did not verify DO-178C with DO-330 tool qualification, and the glossary likewise lists both standards as unverified [f7633, f15369]. The glossary extends that verification gap to MIL-STD-3022, so the standards are described as reference frameworks rather than verified foundations for this research [f14664, f14653].
